gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured current draw for radar parking mode. DashCamTalk user SafeDriveSolutions bench-measured the Thinkware U3000 at 16 mA in radar mode at 13.8 V, against 230–250 mA in time-lapse parking and 260–270 mA in motion-detection parking (Jun 7, 2023).
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages. Thinkware's RADAR Parking Mode help article gives the 1–5 m range in five steps, 24 GHz, the under-20 km/h limit and 20 s clips, but no power figure; it only says 'energy-efficient'. Digital Camera World's U3000 Pro review (Alistair Charlton, 2026-01-29) calls the camera 'surprisingly energy-efficient' and says the car battery showed no low-voltage problem, but gives no mA or W figure. The Tom's Guide review, my fetch of the Tom's Guide best list and DashCamTalk's U3000 Pro page (2026-01-17) showed no current or power figure either; the Tom's Guide body was cut off when I fetched it. ChatGPT's answer only says 'low-power standby'. None of them puts a measured number on how much less radar mode draws than buffered or time-lapse parking.
decides: It backs the reason to buy radar at all: on SafeDriveSolutions' bench, a U3000 in radar mode drew about 15 times less current than in time-lapse parking (16 mA ≈ 0.22 W against 230–250 mA ≈ 3.2–3.5 W at 13.8 V). That supports the Thinkware U3000 / U3000 Pro as the pick for long unattended parking. It cannot rank DDPAI against Thinkware. I found no named third-party measurement of the DDPAI radar accessory's draw, range or wake time, only DDPAI's own claims, which I could not open on its pages. DDPAI's place on the page (N5 Pro or N5 Dual 2026 with the $80 radar accessory) has to rest on price and specs, not on measured parking efficiency. A second user reading of the U3000 at 82 mA from a battery-pack app also argues for wording the 16 mA figure as one bench test, not a spec.

findings.label: Radar parking mode current draw (bench)
findings.note: Measured by SafeDriveSolutions, post #1, 2023-06-07. Bench supply Pyramid PSV 150 at 13.8 V, Snap-on EEDM525ECF multimeter (post #3). Front + rear setup is not stated. Watts are my arithmetic: 0.016 A × 13.8 V = 0.22 W.

findings.label: Time-lapse parking current draw (bench)
findings.note: Same SafeDriveSolutions bench test, 2023-06-07. Radar mode (16 mA) is about 14–16× lower; ratio is my arithmetic (230/16 to 250/16).

findings.label: Motion-detection parking current draw (bench)
findings.note: Same SafeDriveSolutions bench test, 2023-06-07. This is the buffered video-triggered mode that radar replaces.

findings.label: Energy Saving parking mode current draw (bench)
findings.note: Same SafeDriveSolutions test, 2023-06-07. Energy Saving records on impact only, with no approach detection, so it draws less than radar but does not capture someone walking up to the car.

findings.label: Radar parking mode current draw (owner, app reading)
findings.note: HUMMER_EV, post #13, 2025-02-22. Read from the iVolt Extra battery-pack app, not a multimeter; no voltage stated. About 5× the 16 mA bench figure; the thread does not explain the gap. Use it to qualify the 16 mA figure as one test.

findings.label: Radar parking field test (no meter)
findings.value: No low-voltage problem and car started normally after a few dozen rain-triggered clips in one night
findings.source_title: Thinkware U3000 Pro review – Digital Camera World
findings.note: Alistair Charlton, 2026-01-29, powered by the OBD-II cable. He found the default radar sensitivity too high, so rain woke the camera; one notch lower helped. No current or watt figure given. This is a cited rival page.

findings.source_title: RADAR Parking Mode – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: Maker figure, already on a cited rival page. Rear range is measured from the rear camera, not the bumper; Thinkware's example of a camera 1.5 m from the rear end leaves 1.5 m of effective range at Mid.
